pending_selection.name: pivot
pending_selection.confirm_first: Re-read IDEAS.md section 4 before any implementation. Sleep-on-it rule.
pending_selection.hook_sentence: Finds the way to turn your sofa through the door - or proves there isn't one, and names the centimetre that would fix it.
pending_selection.description: Plans how to move furniture through tight spaces, or proves it cannot.

behaviour_descriptor.interaction_model: describe a space and an object, watch the move

pending_selection.definition_of_done: pivot is done when a person can describe a real space - a 2D floor plan, or a stairwell given as a handful of measurements - together with a real object, and get back one of exactly three answers, each carrying evidence they can check themselves. First: a motion, given as the sequence of positions and rotations that gets the object through, animated, and written out as instructions a person can follow, certified collision-free by exact arithmetic rather than by sampling. Second: a proof that no motion exists, showing the pinch point and the smallest dimensional change that would make it possible. Third: an explicit 'too tight to decide' when the geometry falls inside the solver's stated resolution limit - it never guesses. Done requires the 2D case fully certified, the 3D case working for box-shaped objects through stairwells with tilt, a demo that runs in a browser with no install, and a test suite that includes analytic controls (the closed-form longest-rod-around-a-corner result) and randomised differential tests against a brute-force checker. Not done until a stranger can run it on their own doorway from the README alone.

open_questions_for_milestone_1: Certificate scheme for a free motion: exact clearance at sampled configurations plus a Lipschitz bound on point displacement along each segment, so a whole segment is certified rather than a set of poses.

Certificate scheme for blockage: a cover of configuration space by boxes each proven entirely colliding, plus separation of start and goal in the free-space graph. Termination is not guaranteed for near-degenerate geometry - that case must report 'too tight to decide' instead of guessing.

Keeping arithmetic exact under rotation: rational parameterisation of the rotation (tangent half-angle) keeps cos and sin rational, so the whole pipeline can stay in fractions.Verify this survives the clearance computation before committing to it.
Configuration-space representation and search order over (x, y, theta).
